findings.reason: In published proof steps 3.1 and 4.1, the proof uses thm-the-lebesgue-integral-respects-almost-everywhere-equality to transfer integrals for nonnegative functions that may have infinite integral, and to conclude g is in L1 before establishing that fact. That supplier only applies when both functions are already in L1. The smallest missing result is almost-everywhere invariance for extended nonnegative integrals, or an independent proof via simple approximations. The assigned consumer is ex-nonconforming-residual-breaks-galerkin-orthogonality, step 2.1; reviewed published consumers also include lem-square-integrable-kernels-define-bounded-compact-integral-operators, steps 1.1 and 5.1, and lem-conjugate-transpose-kernels-give-adjoints, steps 1.1 and 2.1.

Proof step 3.1 uses the Riemann/Darboux additivity supplier to sum cell integrals for an L2 Lebesgue norm. Make the finite-cell Lebesgue integral decomposition explicit, or establish the required Riemann/Lebesgue identification for this piecewise-continuous integrand.

Proof step 1.2 splits the exact Lebesgue form integral and global gradient L2 norms over the finite measurable partition without stating the finite-additivity step and the needed integrability. Make that partition argument explicit before applying the cellwise bounds.

Approved NA-30 scope calls for family estimates under uniform discrete stability and controlled consistency and approximation terms. This theorem gives only a per-mesh bound, unlike the first-Strang theorem's explicit family consequence. Add the corresponding uniform-family consequence, stating uniform bounds on M_h, a positive lower bound on alpha_h, and control of the approximation and residual terms.
